findings.claim: The three positive secrecy/authentication results describe an executing adversarial-review protocol.
findings.observation: All receivers lie in the continuation after the first private output. Under synchronous private communication the initial output cannot rendezvous; protocol roles never run. ProVerif returns all three original queries true, but added reachability queries cannot reconstruct traces.
findings.qualification: Deadlock is a source-level process-semantics argument. ProVerif says cannot be proved for reachability, not proved unreachable. This is a vacuity/model-initialization finding, not a cryptographic break.
findings.response: Instantiate the roles in parallel with private parameters. Concrete traces now witness red publication, defense publication and defense learning; seeded plaintext leaks produce attacks.
findings.title: Private initialization precedes every receiving process

findings.claim: Both the defense publisher and Gate-B receiver participate in one round.
findings.observation: After parallelizing private key distribution, only one defense role can consume the sole key tuple. A joint DefenseWrites-and-DefenseLearnsRed marker has no reconstructable trace; providing a second tuple produces a concrete joint trace.
findings.qualification: This latent modeling bug is exposed after fixing R1-RED-001. Non-reachability follows from one-send/two-consumer resource counting; ProVerif does not itself prove non-reachability here.
findings.response: Give the publisher and receiver their own defense-key parameters. One joint trace witnesses both roles participating in the same execution.
findings.title: One defense-key send cannot provision two consuming roles

findings.claim: White receives red plaintext only after the attack manifest has been sealed.
findings.observation: In the live-provisioning variant, insert AttackManifestSealed immediately after the red output and ask DefenseLearnsRed(red_msg) ==> AttackManifestSealed. ProVerif returns false with a concrete trace; original S1/S2/S3 still hold. The lead can relay the first ciphertext before the red continuation seals.
findings.qualification: Counterexample applies to the instrumented, operational repaired harness and the stronger lifecycle claim. The original S3 is only source authentication; no claim of an exploit in a deployed daemon.
findings.response: Bind a domain-separated seal signature to the manifest identity and ciphertext. The lead verifies the seal before release; correspondences check seal, release and learning order.
findings.title: Authenticated lead emission does not enforce seal-before-delivery

items.summary: **(a) Verdict: partially known.** Supervisory control under observation and control delay is a mature subfield with an exact characterization. Feng Lin (SIAM J. Control Optim. 52(2):1276–1298, 2014, DOI 10.1137/130914942) models delays and losses with observation mappings and defines **network controllability** and network observability, which "capture precisely the requirements on effective supervisory control in networked discrete event systems."\[1\]\[2\] Shu & Lin and others give synthesis algorithms. Basin, Jugé, Klaedtke & Zălinescu ("Enforceable Security Policies Revisited," ACM TISSEC 16(1):3, 2013, DOI 10.1145/2487222.2487225) partition actions into **controllable** and **only-observable** ones.\[3\]\[4\] They characterize enforceability as (U,O)-safety, informally "P is safety and bad things are not caused by an only-observable action", and apply it to timing constraints.\[3\]\[5\] Not stated anywhere: a **lease deadline** as the controllable timeout that makes a delayed policy enforceable.

items.summary: **(a) Verdict: partially known.** Attenuation-only semantics are the design invariant of Macaroons (NDSS 2014: caveats "attenuate and contextually confine," and removing or reordering a caveat breaks the HMAC chain), Biscuit and UCAN.\[9\]\[10\] The 2026 IETF individual draft draft-niyikiza-oauth-attenuating-agent-tokens-00 states a "capability monotonicity invariant (I4)" and depth monotonicity (I2), with chain verification that "enforces the monotonic attenuation invariant at each delegation step."\[11\] That is per-hop checking stated as an invariant, not as a lattice theorem. Lattice access models are classical (Denning 1976; Sandhu 1993). I found **no** statement of "per-hop verification ⇔ descending chain in the product lattice (rights × TTL), with root-vs-leaf checking unsound." I also found none naming the A:write → B:read → C:write re-escalation as an endpoint-check failure. Macaroon verification exists only at the cryptographic level (López-Alt, NYU TR2013-962, verified).\[12\] I found no Tamarin or ProVerif model of chain monotonicity.

items.summary: ## D5. Quantity versus semantics of leakage through a gate

items.classification: source-asserted recommendation or literature statement; adjudication in direction disposition

items.summary: **(a) Verdict: already known (quantity) / partially known (semantics).** Smith ("Quantifying information flow using min-entropy," QEST 2011) proves Theorem 3.3: "If C is deterministic, then its min-capacity is the logarithm of the number of feasible outputs." He also proves Theorem 3.4: "the min-capacity of a cascade cannot exceed the min-capacity of either link."\[13\] Laundering t = f(s) followed by an honest g(t) is such a cascade, so leakage is ≤ log₂|range(g)| ≤ b bits per job regardless of f. The "miracle theorem" (Alvim, Chatzikokolakis, Palamidessi & Smith, CSF 2012, Thm 5.1) gives g-capacity ≤ min-capacity for every gain function.\[14\] Shannon capacity ≤ log|Y|.\[15\] So the q·b ledger is a **known-correct upper bound** under all three measures. The semantic residual is the "**what**" dimension of Sabelfeld & Sands' taxonomy (JCS 2009), formalized by delimited release's "escape hatches" (Sabelfeld & Myers). Robust declassification (Zdancewic & Myers 2001) addresses attacker influence over what is released.

items.classification: source-asserted recommendation or literature statement; adjudication in direction disposition

items.summary: **(a) Verdict: partially known.** The worst-case dependence bound is classical. By Fréchet–Hoeffding, P(all k miss) ∈ [max(0, kβ − (k−1)), β], so power lies between **1 − β** (comonotone misses) and min(1, k(1−β)). Under positive association (Harris–FKG), P(all miss) ≥ β^k, so 1 − β^k is an **upper** bound on power that is valid only under independence. A 2026 agent paper says exactly this: "If an attacker leaks one visible credential string and that string is a honeytoken, the detection probability is 1−β, not 1−β^k" (arXiv 2606.04141, "Caught in the Act(ivation)," with DP honeytoken generation and conformal calibration).\[17\] Related work: "Kill-Chain Canaries" (arXiv 2603.28013) tracks a SECRET-[A-F0-9]{8} canary through exposed/persisted/relayed/executed stages, and arXiv 2507.15613 uses decoy secrets.\[18\]\[19\] I found no application of non-adaptive group-testing designs to canary *placement*.

items.summary: **(a) Verdict: partially known (provisional; no searches were budgeted).** Blackwell (1953) shows that E dominates F for all decision problems iff F is a garbling of E. Le Cam's deficiency δ(E,F) (1964) is the worst-case excess risk over bounded losses, which is exactly a "decision price of a digest," and it is a linear program for finite experiments. Rate-distortion with d(x,a) = loss (Shannon 1959; "task-oriented" compression) gives the minimal *average* bits. Frankel & Kamenica (2019) value information via decision problems. I found no zero-error, worst-case combinatorial counterpart. The covering bound log₂C(N,k) − log₂C(m,k) sits at the δ = 0, 0-1-loss corner.

items.summary: ## D25. Locating colluding equivocators via graph codes

items.classification: source-asserted recommendation or literature statement; adjudication in direction disposition
items.status: Retain exact source; use linked direction obligations and existing task status. No assertion is promoted by intake.
items.summary: **(a) Verdict: already known, with a framing correction.** The cycle space of a connected graph is a binary [m, m−n+1, g] code with g the girth (Hakimi & Bredeson, IEEE TIT 14:584–591, 1968; decoding by Bredeson & Hakimi, IEEE TIT 13:348–349, 1967).\[42\]\[43\] A distance-d code corrects ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors. **Correction:** consistent witness data is a *coboundary*, and the cycles are **parity checks**. An undetectable edge-error pattern is itself a coboundary, i.e., lies in the **cut space**. The relevant distance is therefore the minimum cut, λ(G), not the girth, and "two liars cancel" means their combined error forms a cut. So ≤ t edge-level equivocations are locatable iff λ(G) ≥ 2t+1, matching power-grid bad-data identifiability (critical measurements; unverified textbook source). Robinson's consistency radius "places a lower bound on the amount of distortion incurred by the fusion process" (Information Fusion 2017; arXiv 1603.01446), which is the manuscript's single-liar bound.\[44\]\[45\] Sheng et al. (CCS 2021) prove the number of identifiable culpable replicas is "either 0 or as large as t+1," and that for n = 2t+1 under synchrony forensic support is "inherently nonexistent."\[46\]\[47\]

An SBES 2026 study of 14,960 conflicting internal merges in 12,299 AI-authored PRs found agents rarely resolve their own conflicts, with self-resolution rates differing "by nearly 60× across vendors."\[69\] MAST (Cemri et al., NeurIPS 2025 D&B; 150 traces, κ = 0.88; 1,642 annotated traces) names step repetition, loss of conversation history and information withholding, which are qualitative analogues of duplicate work and lost state.\[66\]\[70\] Base dataset: AIDev (arXiv 2507.15003), with 456,535 agent PRs across 61,453 repositories.\[71\]
